title: French Revolution & Age of Enlightenment
description: Comprehensive 60-question historical journey through 1789, the Bastille, the Reign of Terror, the Directory, and the rise of Napoleon.

questions.question: In what month and year was the storming of the Bastille fortress in Paris?
questions.explanation: The storming of the Bastille occurred on 14 July 1789, symbolizing the collapse of absolute royal authority.

questions.question: Which French monarch was executed by guillotine at the Place de la Révolution in January 1793?
questions.explanation: King Louis XVI was convicted of high treason by the National Convention and executed on 21 January 1793.

questions.question: What landmark document was adopted by the National Constituent Assembly in August 1789?
options: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
questions.explanation: Adopted on 26 August 1789, the Declaration established core human and civil liberties.

questions.question: Who was the influential Jacobin lawyer who led the Committee of Public Safety during the Reign of Terror?
questions.explanation: Maximilien Robespierre headed the revolutionary government during the height of the Terror (1793–1794).

questions.question: Who assassinated the radical journalist Jean-Paul Marat in his medicinal bath in July 1793?
questions.explanation: Charlotte Corday, a Girondin sympathizer from Normandy, assassinated Marat to curb factional violence.

questions.question: In what year was the Estates-General convened at Versailles for the first time since 1614?
questions.explanation: Louis XVI summoned the Estates-General in May 1789 to address catastrophic state debts.

questions.question: What pledge did deputies of the Third Estate swear in June 1789 after being locked out of their hall?
questions.explanation: The deputies gathered on an indoor tennis court (Jeu de Paume) promising not to separate until France had a written constitution.

questions.question: Which queen of France, wife of Louis XVI, was executed in October 1793?
questions.explanation: Queen Marie Antoinette of Austria was guillotined nine months after her husband.

questions.question: What famous Parisian women's march in October 1789 forced the royal family to relocate to the Tuileries Palace?
questions.explanation: Working-class Parisian women marched to Versailles demanding bread and escorted the royal family back to Paris.

questions.question: Which moderate political faction in the National Convention was purged and eliminated by the Montagnards in 1793?
questions.explanation: The Girondins represented provincial interests and opposed the extreme centralized measures of the Paris Commune.

questions.question: What device was adopted by the National Assembly as the official, uniform instrument of capital punishment?
questions.explanation: Proposed by Dr. Joseph-Ignace Guillotin, the mechanical blade was intended to deliver rapid and egalitarian executions.

questions.question: In what year was Maximilien Robespierre overthrown and guillotined during the Thermidorian Reaction?
questions.explanation: The 9th of Thermidor Year II (27 July 1794) brought down Robespierre and marked the end of the Reign of Terror.

questions.question: What radical Enlightenment philosopher authored "The Social Contract" in 1762?
questions.explanation: Rousseau argued that sovereignty resides with the people and their general will.

questions.question: Which Enlightenment satirist wrote "Candide" and campaigned fiercely against religious intolerance?
questions.explanation: François-Marie Arouet, known as Voltaire, was a champion of free expression, religious freedom, and civil rights.

questions.question: Who served as the chief co-editor of the monumental 28-volume "Encyclopédie" published from 1751 to 1772?
questions.explanation: Denis Diderot spearheaded the compilation of the Encyclopédie to diffuse secular, empirical knowledge.

questions.question: Which French political philosopher formulated the theory of the separation of powers in "The Spirit of the Laws"?
questions.explanation: Montesquieu proposed dividing governmental power among executive, legislative, and judicial branches.

questions.question: What was the three-word national motto popularized during the French Revolution?
questions.explanation: Liberty, Equality, Fraternity became the enduring rallying cry and official motto of the French Republic.

questions.question: In what year did Napoleon Bonaparte launch the Coup of 18 Brumaire, establishing the French Consulate?
questions.explanation: On 9 November 1799 (18 Brumaire Year VIII), General Napoleon Bonaparte toppled the Directory and became First Consul.

questions.question: What revolutionary song composed by Claude Joseph Rouget de Lisle in 1792 became France's national anthem?
questions.explanation: Originally titled "Chant de guerre pour l'Armée du Rhin", it became known as La Marseillaise when volunteer troops entered Paris singing it.

questions.question: What was the name of the paper currency issued by the revolutionary government backed by confiscated Church property?
questions.explanation: Assignats suffered massive hyperinflation and depreciation throughout the early 1790s.

questions.question: Which social group of working-class Parisian radicals was recognized by their long trousers instead of aristocratic breeches?
questions.explanation: Sans-culottes literally translates to "without short breeches", identifying working-class militants.

questions.question: What failed royal escape attempt occurred in June 1791 when the royal family fled toward the Austrian border?
questions.explanation: The royal carriage was intercepted and recognized at the town of Varennes-en-Argonne and escorted back under guard.

questions.question: Which French playwright and feminist activist authored the "Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen" in 1791?
questions.explanation: Olympe de Gouges challenged male authority and was guillotined during the Terror in November 1793.

questions.question: In what year was Napoleon Bonaparte crowned Emperor of the French at Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris?
questions.explanation: On 2 December 1804, Napoleon took the crown in the presence of Pope Pius VII and crowned himself Emperor.

questions.question: What revolutionary civil religion did Maximilien Robespierre inaugurate with a massive festival in June 1794?
questions.explanation: The Cult of the Supreme Being was intended to replace both Catholicism and the atheistic Cult of Reason.

questions.question: What body of law promulgated under Napoleon in 1804 unified French jurisprudence and spread across Europe?
questions.explanation: The Code Civil des Français established equality before the law, freedom of religion, and property rights.

questions.question: Which major French naval defeat against Britain in October 1805 ended French plans to invade England?
questions.explanation: Admiral Lord Nelson's Royal Navy defeated the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar.

questions.question: What decisive battle in December 1805 is considered Napoleon's tactical masterpiece, defeating Austrian and Russian armies?
questions.explanation: Also known as the Battle of the Three Emperors, Austerlitz destroyed the Third Coalition.

questions.question: What was the five-member executive committee that governed France from 1795 to 1799 called?
questions.explanation: The Directoire ruled under the Constitution of Year III until overthrown by Napoleon in 1799.

questions.question: In what year did Napoleon invade Russia with the Grande Armée of over 600,000 soldiers?
questions.explanation: The disastrous Russian campaign of 1812 decimated Napoleon's forces through scorched-earth tactics and winter.

questions.question: Where was Napoleon exiled after his first abdication in April 1814?
questions.explanation: Napoleon was granted sovereignty over the Mediterranean island of Elba before escaping back to France in 1815.

questions.question: Which final battle in June 1815 ended Napoleon's Hundred Days return to power?
questions.explanation: Anglo-Allied forces under the Duke of Wellington and Prussian forces under Blücher defeated Napoleon in modern Belgium.

questions.question: Where was Napoleon permanently exiled until his death in 1821?
questions.explanation: Saint Helena is a remote volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean controlled by the British Empire.

questions.question: What European diplomatic conference in 1814–1815 redrew the political boundaries of Europe following the Napoleonic Wars?
questions.explanation: Chaired by Klemens von Metternich, the Congress restored conservative royal balances of power.

questions.question: Who was the Bourbon king restored to the throne of France after the fall of Napoleon in 1814?
questions.explanation: Louis XVIII, the younger brother of executed Louis XVI, ruled France during the Bourbon Restoration.

questions.question: In what year did Napoleon die in exile at Longwood House on Saint Helena?
questions.explanation: Napoleon Bonaparte died on 5 May 1821 at the age of 51.

questions.question: What revolutionary calendar replaced the Gregorian calendar from 1793 to 1805?
questions.explanation: The calendar featured 12 months named after seasonal characteristics (like Thermidor, Brumaire, and Floreal).

questions.question: What metric measurement system reform was formally adopted in France during the Revolution in 1795?
options: Metric System based on the metre and kilogram
questions.explanation: The French National Convention established the decimal metric system to standardize measurements nationally and internationally.

questions.question: Which prominent chemist was executed during the Reign of Terror despite his foundational work in stoichiometry?
questions.explanation: Antoine Lavoisier, known as the father of modern chemistry, was executed due to his past role as a royal tax farmer (Ferme générale).

questions.question: Which Caribbean colony launched a successful anti-slavery revolution inspired by French republican ideals in 1791?
questions.explanation: Led by Toussaint Louverture, the Haitian Revolution resulted in the world's first free Black republic in 1804.

questions.question: In what year did the National Convention officially abolish slavery throughout all French colonies for the first time?
questions.explanation: On 4 February 1794 (16 Pluviôse Year II), the Convention emancipated all enslaved peoples across French territories.

questions.question: In what year did the French Revolution officially begin with the convening of the Estates-General and Bastille storming?
questions.explanation: The outbreak of the French Revolution is universally dated to the year 1789.

questions.question: What famous neoclassical painter served as the official visual propagandist of the Revolution and painted "The Death of Marat"?
questions.explanation: Jacques-Louis David painted iconic revolutionary artworks and later became the First Painter to Emperor Napoleon.

questions.question: What was the name of the political club where Maximilien Robespierre and Saint-Just met in a former Dominican convent?
questions.explanation: The Society of the Friends of the Constitution was called the Jacobin Club after the Saint-Jacques Dominican monastery.

questions.question: Who was the energetic orator and member of the Committee of Public Safety who was guillotined along with his allies in April 1794?
questions.explanation: Georges Danton advocated for leniency to wind down the Terror, leading Robespierre to send him to the guillotine.

questions.question: Which royal fortress and palace in Paris was stormed by armed insurrectionists on 10 August 1792, ending the monarchy?
questions.explanation: The insurrection of 10 August 1792 overthrew Louis XVI and led directly to the declaration of the First French Republic.

questions.question: What was the conservative reaction following the fall of Robespierre in July 1794 named after the revolutionary month?
questions.explanation: The Thermidorian Reaction repealed price controls and dismantled the apparatus of the Terror.

questions.question: How many days were there in each decade (week) of the French Republican Calendar?
questions.explanation: The Republican calendar decimalized time: every month had three 10-day weeks called décades.

questions.question: Which British political thinker published the conservative critique "Reflections on the Revolution in France" in 1790?
questions.explanation: Edmund Burke predicted that violent revolutionary rupture would degenerate into tyranny and military dictatorship.

questions.question: Which Anglo-American radical responded to Burke by publishing "Rights of Man" in 1791 defending the French Revolution?
questions.explanation: Thomas Paine defended democratic principles and was later made an honorary French citizen and deputy.

questions.question: What military campaign in 1798–1801 led by Napoleon aimed to disrupt British trade routes to India and uncovered the Rosetta Stone?
options: French expedition to Egypt and Syria
questions.explanation: Napoleon's expedition to Egypt included a corps of 167 scientists and scholars whose discoveries birthed modern Egyptology.

questions.question: What economic blockade system instituted by Napoleon in 1806 prohibited trade between continental Europe and Britain?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Decree established the Continental Blockade to strangle the British economy through commercial embargo.

questions.question: What prolonged and bloody guerrilla conflict in Spain and Portugal severely drained French military resources from 1808 to 1814?
questions.explanation: Napoleon referred to the brutal guerrilla resistance across the Iberian Peninsula as his "Spanish Ulcer".

questions.question: In what year was the historic Battle of Waterloo fought near Brussels, Belgium?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Waterloo took place on Sunday, 18 June 1815.

questions.question: What mass public trials court operated in Paris to sentence political suspects during the Terror?
questions.explanation: The Revolutionary Tribunal tried thousands of political prisoners with minimal rights to legal defense.

questions.question: Which French royalist insurrection broke out in western France in 1793 against conscription and anti-clerical laws?
questions.explanation: The Vendée uprising resulted in severe civil war and military suppression by republican armies.

questions.question: What Enlightenment philosopher published "The Spirit of the Laws" in 1748?
questions.explanation: Montesquieu's work analyzed political structures and advocated check-and-balance systems.

questions.question: Which prominent mathematician and philosopher authored the "Sketch for a Historical Picture of the Progress of the Human Spirit"?
questions.explanation: Condorcet championed egalitarianism, public education, and human progress before dying during the Terror.

questions.question: What landmark legal agreement in 1801 restored relations between the French government and the Roman Catholic Church?
questions.explanation: Signed by Napoleon and Pope Pius VII, the Concordat restored public Catholic worship while retaining state supremacy.

questions.question: How many total articles were in the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen adopted in 1789?
questions.explanation: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen contains exactly 17 foundational articles.
